<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Chairman&#146;s Letter</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Dear Shareholder, </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s
Investor Shares returned 4.8% in 2005 as U.S. stocks made overall gains for the third
straight year. The fund&#146;s lower-cost Admiral Shares returned 4.9%. The fund closely
tracked the 4.9% return of its benchmark, the Standard &amp; Poor&#146;s 500 Index, and
equaled the 4.8% average return of its peer fund group.</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The first table on page 1 provides the
total returns (capital change plus reinvested distributions) for both of the fund&#146;s
share classes and its comparative measures. The per-share components of the fund&#146;s
total returns&#151;starting and ending net asset values, as well as income
distributions&#151;are shown in the second table. Shareholders who own the 500 Index Fund
in a taxable account may also wish to review the fund&#146;s after-tax returns on page 27.
If you held the fund in a taxable account, you&#146;ll note that the fund did not
distribute capital gains for the sixth straight year. In addition, the fund&#146;s
dividend distributions met the test for qualified dividend income, which is eligible for a
reduced tax rate. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The U.S. stock market was
quiet even as returns spiked elsewhere </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The performance of the U.S. stock market was subdued in 2005. After retreating at the start of the year, stock prices meandered upward, and the broad U.S. market returned 6.3% for the 12 months. Differences
between the returns of small-</FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>2 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 3; page: 3" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<br><br>





<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>and large-capitalization stocks, and
of value- and growth-oriented stocks, were relatively narrow. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>International stocks generated
excellent returns. Stocks from emerging markets and the Pacific region, particularly those
listed on the Japanese stock exchange, were standouts. Crude oil and natural gas prices
rose 41% and 58%, respectively, applying pressure, but not a choke hold, to the U.S.
economy. The prices of metals and other commodities also surged. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Modest bond returns
belied unusual interest rate movements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During 2005, the Federal Reserve Board
boosted its target for short-term interest rates to 4.25%, from 2.25%. The yields of most
fixed-income securities followed suit. Increases were most pronounced among short-term
investments. Among longer-term securities, the increase was modest. (In fact, the yield of
the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond declined slightly.) </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Toward the end of 2005, these unusual
dynamics led to an inversion of the yield curve, with short-term bonds yielding slightly
more than some long-term bonds. Because rising yields are the flip side of falling bond
prices, these interest rate movements also meant weak 12-month returns for short-term
bonds and better performance from intermediate- and long-term securities. The broad
taxable bond market returned 2.4% for the year. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Directionless at first,
the S&amp;P 500 went on to advance modestly </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#151;like the
target S&amp;P 500 itself&#151;drifted sideways through the first half of the year, and
the Investor Shares finished the first six months with a &#150;0.9% return. However,
investors grew more positive about stocks as the summer progressed. Your fund posted
consecutive quarterly gains of 3.6% and 2.0%, which helped it to close 2005 with returns
approaching 5%. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund&#146;s advance, if not
dramatic, was broadly based, reflecting gains in most market sectors. The leading industry
by far was energy (+31.3%)&#151;no surprise given the prominence of rising oil and gas
prices during the year. Although energy stocks make up less than 10% of the index,
&#147;big oil&#148; firms such as ExxonMobil (+12%), the market&#146;s second-largest
company by capitalization, and ConocoPhillips (+37%) provided outsized increases. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Most other S&amp;P 500 sectors
advanced, with financials (the largest sector by market value) and health care gaining
6.5% each. Utilities (+16.8%) also more than pulled their weight. Investors in information
technology stocks (+1%), the index&#146;s second-largest group, continued to sort through
winners and losers in the fast-moving industry. Illustrating the sector&#146;s volatility,
the fund&#146;s leading gainers included computer makers Apple (+123%) and Hewlett-Packard
(+38%), while the two stocks exerting the biggest drag on the fund&#146;s performance were
computer giant Dell (&#150;29%) and venerable IBM (&#150;16%). </FONT></P>

Warner (&#150;10%), and News Corp. (&#150;16%). The other sector that declined was
telecommunications services (&#150;5.6%). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The 500 Index Fund
possesses a long-term record worth reviewing </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund&#146;s long-term performance
continues to showcase the merits of index investing. As shown in the table on page 4, over
the past decade your fund has returned 9.0% a year, on average&#151;1.7 percentage points
above the average return of competing large-company mutual funds, the vast majority of
which are actively managed. The cumulative effect of this outperformance is illustrated by
the growth of hypothetical $10,000 initial investments in the fund and the average peer;
as you can see, your fund would have ended up $3,446 ahead. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The fund&#146;s advisor,
Vanguard&#146;s Quantitative Equity Group, has provided consistently excellent results in
tracking the performance of the S&amp;P 500 Index. An index is a theoretical portfolio
that incurs no investment expenses, making it a small bull&#146;s-eye to hit. Yet the 500
Index Fund has come very close to doing so, despite its real-world expenses. The
fund&#146;s ten-year annualized return is only one tenth of a percentage point behind that
of the S&amp;P 500 Index&#151;about as close as we can get to replicating its performance.
For an index fund, that result constitutes a resounding success. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>What&#146;s more, the fund&#146;s
competitive advantages, including broad diversification and low turnover, are difficult
for competitor funds to overcome because most of them must surmount much higher operating
expenses in pursuit of superior performance. As you can see in the table on page 4, your
investment continues to benefit from a cost advantage shareholders have enjoyed since the
fund&#146;s inception back in 1976. While we believe that actively managed
funds&#151;especially those with clear mandates, experienced management, and low
costs&#151;have a place in many portfolios, the long-term success of Vanguard 500 Index
Fund is powerful evidence that diversified, low-cost index funds should be core holdings
for most investors. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Experienced investors
recognize the benefits of a long-range strategy </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As long-time Vanguard shareholders
know, we continually urge our clients to focus on long-term performance rather than
short-term trends. Inexperienced investors looking at Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#146;s
performance over the last three years might be tempted to think that this positive trend
will mean more gains in 2006. However, nothing the market did yesterday guarantees what it
will do tomorrow. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>5 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 3; page: 3" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<br><br>




<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>One thing that does stay constant,
though, is the need to keep a long-term perspective. Even if the stocks listed in the
S&amp;P 500 Index&#151;and therefore owned by the fund&#151;should reverse course and post
negative results this year, a buy-and-hold approach will remain the best way for stock
investors to seek long-term growth of capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Patient investors know that time is
their best ally. For example, after three consecutive years of decline in 2000&#150;2002,
the 500 Index Fund still had a ten-year annualized return of 9.3%. Now, after three
consecutive positive years, the fund&#146;s ten-year annualized return remains about 9.0%,
which is the broad market&#146;s annualized return over the past 75 years. The annual ups
and downs get smoothed out by the passage of time, and the market&#146;s long-term results
emerge as the only numbers that count for those who stick with a sound investment plan. We
think the 500 Index Fund is a reliable component of any such plan because it aims to
capture the overall return of companies that make up the bulk of the stock market&#146;s
value, and it does so with the aid of skilled management and consistently low costs. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Naturally, you need more than one
mutual fund to reach your goals. We hope that, no matter what the stock and bond markets
do in 2006, you will maintain a steady and well-diversified mix of stock funds, bond
funds, and short-term reserves designed for your specific circumstances and objectives. I
hope you will take advantage of the many resources we offer at Vanguard.com&reg; that can
help you build and maintain a successful investment program. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered
under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or mutual
fund. The fund offers two classes of shares, Investor Shares and Admiral Shares. Investor
Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase
requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative,
servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New
          York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date.
          Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent,
          with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing
          returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may
          purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or
          sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested
          position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity.
          The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the
          underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively
          than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of
          futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of
          stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility
          of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>3.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>4.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>23 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 3; page: 3" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<br><br>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>5.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional
          borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured
          at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities
          loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity
          Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the
          period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income
          earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>6.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $12,747,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing
          0.01% of the fund&#146;s net assets and 12.74% of Vanguard&#146;s
          capitalization. The fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and
          officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $1,486,508,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

$193,358,000 through December 31, 2008, $890,248,000 through December 31, 2009,

dividend income) and short-term capital gains that became effective as of January 1, 2003,
and on long-term capital gains realized on or after May 6, 2003. To calculate qualified
dividend income, we use actual prior-year figures. (In the example, returns after the sale

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>About Your Fund&#146;s
Expenses</B> </FONT> </H1>

<br><br>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed
as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The
following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of
investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The
examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown
and held for the entire period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table below illustrates your
fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on actual fund
return.</B> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the
period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual
return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an
investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together
with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>To do so, simply divide your account
value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then
multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#147;Expenses
Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on hypothetical 5%
yearly return.</B> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs
with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5%
before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the
return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your
investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and
Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return.
You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the
hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Glossary</B> </FONT> </H1>

<br><br>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Beta.</B>
          A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
          relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
          beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
          would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
          by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
          (see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
          between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
          volatility.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Expense Ratio.</B> The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Median Market Cap.</B> An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B> The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>R-Squared.</B>
          A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
          returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
          fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
          returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
          relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Return on Equity.</B> The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Turnover Rate.</B> An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Yield.</B>
          A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
          expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
          earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
          coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
          provided by securities in the index.</FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>The People Who Govern Your Fund</B> </FONT>


<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><br><br>
The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part

services to them on an at-cost basis.
<br><br>

sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals.
<br><br>
Our independent board members bring distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service to their task of working with Vanguard officers to establish the policies and
oversee the activities of the funds. Among board members&#146; responsibilities are selecting investment advisors for the funds; monitoring fund operations, performance, and costs;
reviewing contracts; nominating and selecting new trustees/directors; and electing Vanguard officers.
<br><br>
Each trustee serves a fund until its termination; or until the trustee&#146;s retirement, resignation, or death; or otherwise as specified in the fund&#146;s
organizational documents. Any trustee may be removed at a shareholders&#146; meeting by a vote representing two-thirds of the net asset value of all shares of
the fund together with shares of other Vanguard funds organized within the same trust. The table on these two pages shows information for each trustee and

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">&gt; For fiscal year 2005, the three
Vanguard small-capitalization index funds produced returns ranging from 6.1% to 8.6%. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">&gt; In the small-cap arena,
growth-oriented stocks outpaced value issues, and the energy and industrials sectors
performed particularly well. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">&gt; All of the funds tracked their
benchmark indexes closely, and two of the three outperformed their average peer-group
competitors by significant margins. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">Chairman&#146;s Letter </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Dear Shareholder, </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>During 2005, all three of the
Vanguard Small-Cap Index Funds tracked their indexes with precision and, like the overall
stock market, recorded positive results. In the small-cap arena, growth-oriented stocks
outperformed their value-oriented counterparts. The returns for two of the three Vanguard
Small-Cap Index Funds were superior to the average returns produced by their peer funds.</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table on page 1 shows the total
returns (capital change plus reinvested distributions) for all the funds&#146; share
classes, as well as for their benchmarks. Further details of the funds&#146; returns,
including income distributions and price changes, appear on page 2. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>If you hold your shares in a taxable
account, you may wish to review the funds&#146; after-tax returns on page 57. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The U.S. stock market was
quiet even as returns spiked elsewhere </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The performance of the U.S. stock
market was subdued in 2005. After retreating at the start of the year, stock prices
meandered upward, and the broad U.S. market returned 6.3% for the 12 months. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>International stocks generated
excellent returns. Stocks from emerging markets and the Pacific region, particularly those
listed on the Japanese stock exchange, were standouts. Crude oil and natural gas prices
rose 41% and 58%, respectively, </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> 3</FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 8; page: 8" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>applying pressure, but not a choke
hold, to the U.S. economy. The prices of metals and other commodities also surged. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Modest bond returns
belied unusual interest rate movements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During 2005, the Federal Reserve Board
boosted its target for short-term interest rates to 4.25%, from 2.25%. The yields of most
fixed-income securities followed suit. Increases were most pronounced among short-term
investments. Among long-term securities, the increase was modest. (In fact, the yield of
the 30-year U.S. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Treasury bond declined slightly.) </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Toward the end of 2005, these unusual
dynamics led to a slight inversion of the yield curve, with short-term bonds yielding
slightly more than some long-term bonds. Because rising yields are the flip side of
falling bond prices, these interest rate movements also meant weak 12-month returns for
short-term bonds and better performance from intermediate- and long-term securities. The
broad taxable bond market returned 2.4% for the year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

the small-cap markets </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During 2005, small-cap stocks
performed well but were unable to duplicate the exceptional performance of the  prior two years. The

provided by Lipper Inc. and capture information through year-end 2004. </FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>5 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 9; page: 9" -->

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>three funds held a different weighting
in the energy sector, which performed particularly well in 2005 and helped to boost
returns for all of the funds. Similarly, the industrials sector, which constituted about
15% of holdings in each of the funds, returned more than 12% for the 12-month period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">Among other notable sector impacts,
the consumer discretionary sector restrained performance. And, as reduced capital spending
slowed technology issues, the information technology sector crimped returns, not only in
the Small-Cap Growth Index Fund as mentioned previously, but also in the Small-Cap Index
Fund. <BR>
<BR><B>The funds&#146; long-term returns illustrate indexing&#146;s value </B><BR>Indexing is a
long-term strategy, and over time the benefits of its market-matching approach become
clear. While there will inevitably be years when the funds&#146; actively managed
competitors perform better, it&#146;s no surprise when index funds outperform their
competition. In 2005, only the Small-Cap Value Index Fund lagged its average peer, and
this by a mere 0.1%. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->

benchmarks. The table also shows what would have become of a hypothetical $10,000 initial
investment </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>in
each. The Small-Cap Index Fund, for example, returned 10.3% a year, on average, which
would have transformed the $10,000 investment into $26,551. Over the shorter period since
their inceptions&#151;a period in which the 2000&#150;2002 bear market figures more
prominently&#151;the Small-Cap Growth and Small-Cap Value Index Funds produced annualized
returns of 7.6% and 9.0%, respectively.</FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table also shows that two of the
three funds trailed the average returns of their peer groups. That is largely because,
until 2003, the funds tracked indexes that did not reflect the small-cap stock market as
it is viewed by active investment managers. Since May 2003, the funds have targeted
indexes from Morgan Stanley Capital International that, in our estimation, better
represent the market from an active investment perspective. We expect that future
differences between the returns of these index funds and those of their actively managed
competitors will depend more on costs than on any other factor. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Such a development should play to one
of the Small-Cap Index Funds&#146; strengths. Our index funds maintain exceptionally low
costs, an advantage that can compound for investors over time. (For a comparison of
expense ratios, see page 5.) For investors who hold the funds in taxable accounts, the
benefits of index funds can be even greater, as the funds&#146; low turnover should result
in fewer realized capital gains. (As it happens, the Small-Cap and Small-Cap Growth Index
Funds have distributed no capital gains since 2000; the Small-Cap Value Index Fund has
distributed none since 2002.) </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>It&#146;s wise to invest
for the long term and ignore market fads </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>No one can predict with any confidence
what will happen in the financial markets in 2006 and beyond. This is precisely why we
always encourage Vanguard shareholders to evaluate their investments from a long-term
perspective. It&#146;s also why we place such high value on what we believe are the keys
to a sound, long-term investment program&#151;namely, balance among stocks, bonds, and
money market funds; a disciplined approach to investment selection; a constancy of purpose
that doesn&#146;t chase market trends; and careful attention to costs. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As an investor, you can best weather
the market&#146;s uncertainties by sticking with a well-planned strategy. Investing in
Vanguard&#146;s small-cap index funds is a smart way to participate in the long-term
potential of this important segment of the overall stock market. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">Notes to Financial
Statements </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares,
Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who
meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.
Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and
servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading
on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>A.
</B>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
policies in preparing its financial statements. </FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.
          Security Valuation:</B> Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the
          New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation
          date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.
          Futures Contracts:</B> The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully
          invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for
          liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts
          instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more
          attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with
          the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
          values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.
          Federal Income Taxes:</B> The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.
          Distributions:</B> Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.
          Security Lending:</B> The fund may lend its securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required
          to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of
          securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>22 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 25; page: 25" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000">Vanguard Small-Cap Index
Fund </FONT> </H1>
<BR>
<BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a
liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan.
Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less
expenses associated with the loan. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.
          Other:</B> Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $1,243,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.24% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes. During the year ended December 31, 2005, the
          fund realized $329,135,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
          redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held
          by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the
          fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from
          accumulated net realized gains to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For tax purposes, at December 31,
2005, the fund had $1,423,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had
available realized losses of $385,074,000 to offset future net capital gains of
$347,890,000 through December 31, 2011, and $37,184,000 through December 31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At December 31, 2005, net unrealized

purchase and $468,154,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">Notes to Financial
Statements </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund
is registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company,
or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Institutional
Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the
fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Institutional Shares are designed for investors
who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million.
VIPER Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased
and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.
          Security Valuation:</B> Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the
          New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation
          date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.
          Futures Contracts:</B> The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully
          invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for
          liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts
          instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more
          attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with
          the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
          values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.
          Federal Income Taxes:</B> The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions:</B> Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.
          Security Lending:</B> The fund may lend its securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required
          to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of
          securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market
          Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during
          the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the
          income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the
          loan.</FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>37 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Vanguard Small-Cap Growth
Index Fund</B> </FONT> </H1>
<BR>
<BR>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6. Other:
          </B>Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $232,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.23% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $45,913,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For tax purposes, at December 31,
2005, the fund had $127,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had
available realized losses of $29,145,000 to offset future net capital gains of $13,814,000
through December 31, 2011, and $15,331,000 through December 31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At December 31, 2005, net unrealized
appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $381,758,000, consisting of
unrealized gains of $460,617,000 on securities that had risen in value since their
purchase and $78,859,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value since
their purchase. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Vanguard Small-Cap Value
Index Fund</B> </FONT> </H1>
<BR>
<BR>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">Notes to Financial
Statements </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, Institutional
Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the
fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Institutional Shares are designed for investors
who meet certain administrative and servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million.
VIPER Shares are listed for trading on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased
and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.
          Security Valuation:</B> Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the
          New York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation
          date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.
          Futures Contracts:</B> The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited
          extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market,
          enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The
          fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the
          market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully
          invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for
          liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts
          instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more
          attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with
          the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market
          values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.
          Federal Income Taxes:</B> The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.
          Distributions:</B> Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.
          Security Lending:</B> The fund may lend its securities to qualified
          institutional borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required
          to be secured at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of
          securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market
          Liquidity Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during
          the period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the
          income earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the
          loan.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>52 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000">Vanguard Small-Cap Value
Index Fund </FONT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1"> </FONT> </H1>
<BR>
<BR>
<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.
          Other:</B> Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $458,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 0.46% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $116,993,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchange fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->

December 31, 2011. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>About Your Fund&#146;s
Expenses</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This
figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you
understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these
costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000
made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period. The table below
illustrates your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on actual fund
return.</B> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the
period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual
return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an
investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together
with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Indent Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>To
do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value
divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under
the heading &#147;Expenses Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on hypothetical 5%
yearly return.</B> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs
with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5%
before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the
return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your
investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and
Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return.
You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the
hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Note that the expenses shown in the
table on page 59 are meant to highlight and help you compare ongoing costs only and do not
reflect any transactional costs or account maintenance fees. They do not include your
fund&#146;s low-balance fee, which is described in the prospectus. If this fee were
applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not charge transaction
fees, such as purchase or redemption fees, nor does it carry a &#147;sales load.&#148; The
calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may
have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of
any purchases or redemptions. You can find more information about the funds&#146;
expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the <I>Financial Statements </I>section of
this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs,
please refer to the appropriate fund prospectus. </FONT></P>

     <TH ALIGN="Left" COLSPAN="2"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000">Six Months Ended December 31, 2005 </FONT></TH>

     <TH><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2></FONT></TH>
     <TH><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2></FONT></TH></TR>
