<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>1 The calculations are based on
expenses incurred in the most recent six-month period. The fund&#146;s annualized
six-month expense ratios for that period are: 0.23% for the Small-Cap Index Fund Investor
Shares, 0.13% for Admiral Shares, 0.08% for Institutional Shares, and 0.10% for VIPER
Shares; 0.23% for the Small-Cap Growth Index Fund Investor Shares, 0.08% for Institutional
Shares, and 0.11% for VIPER Shares; 0.23% for the Small-Cap Value Index Fund Investor
Shares, 0.08% for Institutional Shares, and 0.11% for VIPER Shares. The dollar amounts
shown as &#147;Expenses Paid&#148; are equal to the annualized expense ratio multiplied by
the average account value over the period, multiplied by the number of days in the most
recent six-month period, then divided by the number of days in the most recent 12-month
period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Glossary </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Beta.</B>
          A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
          relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
          beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
          would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
          by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
          (see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
          between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
          volatility.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Earnings Growth Rate</B>. The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. <BR><BR><B>Expense Ratio.</B> The percentage of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay
its annual administrative and advisory expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to
investors. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Foreign Holdings</B>. The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States.<BR><BR> <B>Median Market Cap</B>. An indicator of the
size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market
price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the
fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Price/Book Ratio</B>. The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. <BR><BR>
<B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> The
ratio of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a
fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. <BR><BR><B>R-Squared</B>. A measure of how much of a
fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as
measured by a given index. If a fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with
an index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Return on Equity</B>. The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Short-Term Reserves</B>. The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. <BR><BR><B>Turnover Rate</B>. An indication of the fund&#146;s trading
activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more
likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate
excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.<BR><BR> <B>Yield</B>. A
snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield, expressed as a
percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income earned over the past 30
days and is annualized, or projected forward for the coming year. The index yield is based
on the current annualized rate of income provided by securities in the index. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>The People Who Govern Your Fund</B> </FONT>


<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><br><br>
The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part
owner of the fund. Your fund trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides
services to them on an at-cost basis.
<br><br>
A majority of Vanguard&#146;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the
sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals.
<br><br>
Our independent board members bring distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service to their task of working with Vanguard officers to establish the policies and
oversee the activities of the funds. Among board members&#146; responsibilities are selecting investment advisors for the funds; monitoring fund operations, performance, and costs;
reviewing contracts; nominating and selecting new trustees/directors; and electing Vanguard officers.
<br><br>
Each trustee serves a fund until its termination; or until the trustee&#146;s retirement, resignation, or death; or otherwise as specified in the fund&#146;s
organizational documents. Any trustee may be removed at a shareholders&#146; meeting by a vote representing two-thirds of the net asset value of all shares of
the fund together with shares of other Vanguard funds organized within the same trust. The table on these two pages shows information for each trustee and
executive officer of the fund. The mailing address of the trustees and officers is P.O. Box 876, Valley Forge, PA 19482.
<br><br><br><br> </FONT>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Red">Chairman&#146;s Letter </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Dear Shareholder, </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Red"><B>The broad U.S. stock market ended
2005 with a modest gain of 6.3%, as measured by the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Composite
Index. Mid-capitalization stocks enjoyed significantly higher returns than the broad
market. The Investor Shares of Vanguard Extended Market Index Fund and Vanguard Mid-Cap
Index Fund gained 10.3% and 13.9%, respectively.</B> </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Both funds fulfilled their objectives
of closely tracking their target indexes. While the performance of the Extended Market
Index Fund was in line with that of the average mid-cap core fund, Vanguard Mid-Cap Index
Fund surpassed its average peer fund by more than 3.5 percentage points. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The first table on page 1 provides the
total returns (capital change plus reinvested distributions) for both funds and their
comparative measures. The per-share components of the funds&#146; total
returns&#151;starting and ending net asset values, as well as income
distributions&#151;are shown in the second table. If you hold either fund in a taxable
account, you may also wish to review the funds&#146; after-tax returns on page 45. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The U.S. stock market was
quiet even as returns spiked elsewhere </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The performance of the U.S. stock
market was subdued in 2005. After retreating at the start of the year, stock prices
meandered upward, and the broad U.S. market returned 6.3% for the 12 months. </FONT></P>



<BR><BR><BR>
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> 2  </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="page-break-after:always"> </P>

<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 1; page: 1" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<BR><BR>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>International stocks generated
excellent returns. Stocks from emerging markets and the Pacific region, particularly those
listed on the Japanese stock exchange, were standouts. Crude oil and natural gas prices
rose 41% and 58%, respectively, applying pressure, but not a choke hold, to the U.S.
economy. The prices of metals and other commodities also surged. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Modest bond returns
belied unusual interest rate movements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Federal Reserve Board boosted its
target for short-term interest rates to 4.25% from 2.25% during 2005. The yields of most
fixed income securities followed suit. Increases were most pronounced among short-term
investments. Among long-term securities, the increase was modest. (In fact, the yield of
the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond declined slightly.) </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Toward the end of 2005, these unusual
dynamics led to a slight inversion of the yield curve, with short-term bonds yielding
slightly more than some long-term bonds. Because rising yields are the flip side of
falling bond prices, these interest rate movements also meant weak 12-month returns for
short-term bonds and better performance from intermediate- and long-term securities. The
broad taxable bond market returned 2.4% for the year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Energy and health care
sectors led gains for 2005 </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For both the Extended Market and
Mid-Cap Index Funds, gains in 2005 were spread across a spectrum of industries. However,
the highest returns for both funds came from the energy and health care sectors. Though
these two sectors represented, on average, 20% or less of each fund&#146;s </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Within the Mid-Cap Index Fund, for
example, the energy sector represented only 10% of holdings but contributed over one-third
of the fund&#146;s overall performance. The fund had much larger holdings in the
financials, consumer discretionary, and information technology sectors, but their impact
on performance was limited, with positive but comparatively modest returns. Like the
energy sector, the health care sector also experienced outsized returns, up 22% for the
year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For the Extended Market Index Fund,
the two largest sectors, on average, were financials (25%) and consumer discretionary
stocks (18%). Returns from financials were subdued, while the fund&#146;s consumer
discretionary sector ended the year with a loss. Once again, energy and health care sector
holdings, although they represented less of the portfolio, carried the day, contributing
about half of the fund&#146;s return. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year, the Extended Market
Index Fund finished the transition of its target benchmark to the S&amp;P Completion
Index. This process began in June and was completed in mid-September. The S&amp;P
Completion Index incorporates several index-construction methodologies favored by Vanguard
Quantitative Equity Group, the fund&#146;s manager. The fund&#146;s objectives and risks
are unchanged. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>This is a significant accomplishment,
given that indexes bear none of the costs that detract from a mutual fund&#146;s return.
It&#146;s an achievement that reflects two competitive advantages: first, the expertise of
the Vanguard Quantitative Equity Group, which has developed proprietary index-tracking
methodologies and trading strategies; and second, the funds&#146; historically very low
expense ratios. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The table below shows the annualized
returns over ten years for the Investor Shares of the Extended Market Index Fund and since
inception for the Mid-Cap Index Fund. During these periods, the Extended Market Index Fund
lagged its average peer by 2.1 percentage points annually, on average, while the Mid-Cap
Index Fund was ahead by the same margin. The shortfall in the comparative performance of
the Extended Market Index Fund arose largely from the nature of its former target index,
which included a greater proportion of small-cap stocks than competing funds typically
hold. Small-cap stocks lagged larger stocks during most of the 1990s. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>It&#146;s wise to invest
for the long term </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>No one can predict with any confidence
what will happen in the financial markets in 2006 and beyond. This is precisely why we
always encourage Vanguard shareholders to evaluate their investments from a long-term
perspective. It&#146;s also why we place such high value on what we believe are the keys
to a sound long-term investment program&#151;namely, balance among stocks, bonds, and
money market funds; a disciplined approach to investment selection; a constancy of purpose
that doesn&#146;t chase market trends; and careful attention to costs. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As an investor, you can best weather
the market&#146;s uncertainties by sticking with a well-planned strategy. Investing in
Vanguard&#146;s medium-capitalization index funds is a smart way to participate in the
long-term potential of an important segment of the overall stock market. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Thank you for entrusting your assets
to Vanguard. </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN="Right"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="Red">Extended Market Index Fund </FONT></H1>

<BR><BR>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Red">Notes to Financial Statements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Extended Market Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares,
Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who
meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.
Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and
servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading
on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New
          York Stock Exchange (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date.
          Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official
          closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such
          securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest
          quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
          readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events
          occurring before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the
          securities&#146; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of
          trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund
          are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments
          acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or
          using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as
          security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
          independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at
          amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent,
          with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing
          returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may
          purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or
          sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested
          position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity.
          The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the
          underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively
          than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of
          futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of
          stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility
          of an illiquid market. Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily
          settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
          recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts
          are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the
          Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the
          contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional
          borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured
          at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities
          loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</FONT></P>

<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> 21  </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="page-break-after:always"> </P>

<BR><BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a
liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan.
Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less
expenses associated with the loan. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $1,247,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.25% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $277,153,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For tax purposes, at December 31,
2005, the fund had $8,886,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had
available realized losses of $100,436,000 to offset future net capital gains through
December 31, 2011. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At December 31, 2005, net unrealized

consisting of unrealized gains of $3,334,978,000 on securities that had risen in value
since their purchase and $1,267,117,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen
in value since their purchase. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN="Right"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="Red">Mid-Cap Index Fund </FONT></H1>
<BR><BR>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Red">Notes to Financial
Statements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Mid-Cap Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares,
Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who
meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.
Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and
servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading
on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>1 </B>Security Valuation:
Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally
4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest
quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each
security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean
of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not
readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring
before the fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary
markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value.
Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#146;s net asset
value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the
latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such
factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by
independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized
cost, which approximates market value. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>2.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent,
          with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing
          returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may
          purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or
          sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested
          position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity.
          The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the
          underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively
          than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of
          futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of
          stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility
          of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>3.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>4.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>5.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional
          borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured
          at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities
          loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</FONT></P>



<BR><BR><BR>
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2> 41  </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="page-break-after:always"> </P>

<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 1; page: 1" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN="Left"><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="Red">Mid-Cap Index Fund </FONT></H1>
<BR><BR>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Liquidity Fund, and records a
liability for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan.
Security lending income represents the income earned on investing cash collateral, less
expenses associated with the loan. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>6.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Each class of shares has equal rights
as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific
expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and
Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses
are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees.
Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $1,497,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.50% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>C.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment
          income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences
          may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among
          capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character.
          Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss
          are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes;
          these differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in
          classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as
          ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $407,157,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. The fund used a tax accounting practice to treat a portion of
the price of capital shares redeemed during the year as distributions from net investment
income. Accordingly, the fund reclassified $6,995,000 from overdistributed net investment
income to paid-in capital. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>For tax purposes, at December 31,
2005, the fund had no ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had available
realized losses of $28,335,000 to offset future net capital gains of $20,314,000 through
December 31, 2011, and $8,021,000 through December 31, 2014. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>At December 31, 2005, net unrealized
appreciation (depreciation) of investment securities for tax purposes was $2,830,426,000,
consisting of unrealized gains of $3,088,961,000 on securities that had risen in value
since their purchase and $258,535,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen
in value since their purchase. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>About Your Fund&#146;s
Expenses</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>As a shareholder of the fund, you
incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative
services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which
are deducted from a fund&#146;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the
fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>A fund&#146;s expenses are expressed
as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The
following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of
investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The
examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown
and held for the entire period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The tables on the next page illustrate
your fund&#146;s costs in two ways: </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on actual fund
return.</B> This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the
period. The &#147;Ending Account Value&#148; shown is derived from the fund&#146;s actual
return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an
investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together
with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>To do so, simply divide your account
value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then
multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#147;Expenses
Paid During Period.&#148; </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>&#149; Based on hypothetical 5%
yearly return.</B> This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#146;s costs
with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5%
before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#151;because the
return used is not the fund&#146;s actual return&#151;the results do not apply to your
investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and
Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return.
You can assess your fund&#146;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the
hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="Red"><B>Glossary</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Beta.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#146;s past share-price fluctuations in
          relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a
          beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically
          would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell
          by 10%. A fund&#146;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared
          (see definition below). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is
          between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of
          volatility.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Earnings Growth Rate.</B> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a
fund. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Expense Ratio.</B> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The percentage
of a fund&#146;s average net assets used to pay its annual administrative and advisory
expenses. These expenses directly reduce returns to investors. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Foreign Holdings.</B> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
percentage of a fund&#146;s equity assets represented by stocks or depositary receipts of
companies based outside the United States. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Median Market Cap.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; An indicator
of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization
(market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#146;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of
the fund&#146;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#146;s
assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Price/Book Ratio.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The share
price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the
weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Price/Earnings Ratio.</B> The ratio
of a stock&#146;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund,
the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market
expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations
for a company&#146;s future growth. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>R-Squared.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          A measure of how much of a fund&#146;s past returns can be explained by the
          returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a
          fund&#146;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#146;s
          returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#146;s returns bore no
          relationship to the index&#146;s returns, its R-squared would be 0.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Return on Equity.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; The annual
average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar
of shareholder&#146;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#146;s equity). For a
fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Short-Term Reserves.</B> The
percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily
converted to cash. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Turnover Rate.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; An indication of
the fund&#146;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction
costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to
investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on
costs. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>Yield.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          A snapshot of a fund&#146;s income from interest and dividends. The yield,
          expressed as a percentage of the fund&#146;s net asset value, is based on income
          earned over the past 30 days and is annualized, or projected forward for the
          coming year. The index yield is based on the current annualized rate of income
          provided by securities in the index.</FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>The People Who Govern Your Fund</B> </FONT>


<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><br><br>
The trustees of your mutual fund are there to see that the fund is operated and managed in your best interests since, as a shareholder, you are a part
owner of the fund. Your fund trustees also serve on the board of directors of The Vanguard Group, Inc., which is owned by the Vanguard funds and provides
services to them on an at-cost basis.
<br><br>
A majority of Vanguard&#146;s board members are independent, meaning that they have no affiliation with Vanguard or the funds they oversee, apart from the
sizable personal investments they have made as private individuals.
<br><br>
Our independent board members bring distinguished backgrounds in business, academia, and public service to their task of working with Vanguard officers to establish the policies and
oversee the activities of the funds. Among board members&#146; responsibilities are selecting investment advisors for the funds; monitoring fund operations, performance, and costs;
reviewing contracts; nominating and selecting new trustees/directors; and electing Vanguard officers.
<br><br>
Each trustee serves a fund until its termination; or until the trustee&#146;s retirement, resignation, or death; or otherwise as specified in the fund&#146;s
organizational documents. Any trustee may be removed at a shareholders&#146; meeting by a vote representing two-thirds of the net asset value of all shares of
the fund together with shares of other Vanguard funds organized within the same trust. The table on these two pages shows information for each trustee and
executive officer of the fund. The mailing address of the trustees and officers is P.O. Box 876, Valley Forge, PA 19482.
<br><br><br><br> </FONT>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">&gt; During the fiscal year ended
December 31, 2005, all four Vanguard large-capitalization index funds closely tracked
their target indexes. </FONT> </P>

<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" COLOR="#FF0000" SIZE="2"><!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" --> </FONT>
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" COLOR="#FF0000" SIZE="2">&gt; The Large-Cap and Value Index
Funds outperformed their peer-group averages for the year, while the Total Stock Market
and Growth Index Funds underperformed their average peers. </FONT> </P>

<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" COLOR="#FF0000" SIZE="2"><!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" --> </FONT>
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" COLOR="#FF0000" SIZE="2">&gt; In a generally subdued year for
equities, value stocks outperformed growth stocks in the large-cap arena. The energy and
utilities sectors did particularly well, while the consumer discretionary and
telecommunication services sectors underperformed. </FONT> </P>

<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Chairman&#146;s Letter</B> </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Dear Shareholder, </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2" COLOR="#FF0000">Pedestrian fourth-quarter returns brought
the U.S. stock market to finish 2005 with a modest gain. The Dow Jones Wilshire 5000
Composite Index, a measure of the broad market, returned 6.3% for the year. </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Like the overall stock market,
Vanguard&#146;s four large-capitalization index funds recorded positive returns in 2005.
All four tracked their target indexes closely, consistent with their objectives. Two of
the funds outperformed their peer-group averages during the year, while two underperformed
their average peers. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The tables on pages 1 and 2 show the
total returns (capital change plus reinvested distributions) for all the funds&#146; share
classes, as well as for their benchmarks. Further details of the funds&#146; returns,
including dividend distributions and price changes, appear on page 3. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>If you hold your shares in a taxable
account, you may wish to review the funds&#146; after-tax returns on page 75. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The U.S. stock market was
quiet even as returns spiked elsewhere </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The performance of the U.S. stock market was subdued in 2005. After retreating at the start of the year, stock prices meandered upward, and the broad U.S. stock market returned 6.3% for the 12 months.
 </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>4 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 1; page: 1" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<br><br>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>International stocks generated
excellent returns. Stocks from emerging markets and the Pacific region, particularly the
Japanese stock exchange, were standouts. Crude oil and natural gas prices rose 41% and
58%, respectively, applying pressure, but not a choke hold, to the U.S. economy. The
prices of metals and other commodities also surged. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Subdued bond returns
belied unusual interest rate movements </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During 2005, the Federal Reserve Board
boosted its target for short-term interest rates to 4.25%, from 2.25%. The yields of most
bonds followed suit. Increases were most pronounced among short-term securities. Among
long-term securities, the increase was modest. (In fact, the yield of the 30-year U.S.
Treasury bond declined slightly.) Toward the end of 2005, these unusual dynamics led to an
inversion of the yield curve, with short-term bonds&#146; yielding slightly more than some
long-term bonds. These interest rate movements also meant weak 12-month returns for
short-term bonds and better performance from intermediate- and long-term securities. The
broad taxable bond market returned 2.4% for the year. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Large-cap value stocks
outpaced their growth counterparts </FONT></H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>An indifferent fourth quarter brought
the four Vanguard large-capitalization index funds to finish 2005 with modest gains,
ranging from 5.1% for the Growth Index Fund to 7.1% for the Value Index Fund. The
broader-based Large-Cap and Total Stock Market Index Funds, which hold both growth stocks
and value stocks, </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>posted returns of 6.1% and 6.0%,
respectively. (All figures are for the funds&#146; Investor Shares.) </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Since energy-related companies tend to
be categorized as value stocks, the Value Index Fund&#146;s return reflected its
comparatively heavy exposure to the energy and utilities sectors, which performed
particularly well in 2005. On the other hand, the Growth Index Fund&#146;s heavier
weightings in the health care and technology sectors restrained the fund&#146;s
performance. The performance of these two sectors, which together accounted for nearly
half of the Growth Index Fund&#146;s average assets, lagged that of the overall market
significantly. Regulatory and clinical-trial challenges hurt the health care sector&#146;s
big pharmaceutical firms, while reduced capital spending by corporations was a drag on
technology issues. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>While the Value Index Fund
outperformed the Growth Index Fund for the past several years, the ten-year performance
chart below shows that the performance difference between the two funds narrows
considerably over longer time periods. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Large-Cap Index Fund, which seeks
to track the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) US Prime Market 750 Index,
essentially combines the holdings of the Growth and Value Index Funds. The 6.1% gain of
the fund&#146;s Investor Shares is precisely at the midpoint between the performance of
the Growth and Value Index Funds&#146; Investor Shares&#151;no surprise given the nature
of the funds&#146; holdings. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>The Total Stock Market Index
Fund&#146;s one-year return of 6.0% for the Investor Shares reflected the fund&#146;s
exposure to the entire market, including the strong relative performance of mid-cap
stocks. The fund&#146;s gains from its large exposure to the financial services sector
were offset by weakness in holdings in the consumer discretionary sector. Among the
fund&#146;s holdings, energy-related companies and utilities posted the best returns, but
their impact on the fund&#146;s overall performance was muted because they accounted for
only about 12% of the fund&#146;s assets. </FONT></P>

<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2"><B>
Indexing's value evidenced by long-term returns</B><br><br>

Indexing is a long-term strategy, and the benefits of its market-matching strategy become crystal clear over time. With this in mind, there will inevitably be years when the funds' actively managed
competitors perform better. Yet even in the short run, it's gratifying when index funds outperform their competition. In 2005, only the Growth Index Fund significantly underperformed the average for its
mutual fund competitors, by about 1 percentage point.<br><br>

As you can see in the table on page 7, indexing consistently proves its value over the long run. During the ten years ended December 31, 2005, a hypothetical $10,000 investment in the Total Stock Market
Index Fund's Investor Shares would have grown to $23,837. The same investment in the average multi-cap core fund would have lagged by nearly $1,000. The Growth, Value, and Large-Cap Index Funds also created
more wealth for their shareholders than their peer-group averages.<br><br>

What are the reasons for this long-term success? First, Vanguard's large-cap index funds are broadly diversified, which minimizes the risk that a few poor-performing stocks will significantly affect
performance. Second, our index funds remain fully invested, so performance doesn't suffer from the drag that uninvested cash can cause in a rising market. Third, the funds' advisor, Vanguard Quantitative
Equity Group, has proven to be among the very best at closely tracking fund benchmarks.<br><br>

Finally, of course, our index funds maintain exceptionally low costs, an advantage that compounds over time. (For a comparison of expense ratios, see page 6.) It's worth noting that, for taxable investors,
the </FONT>
</P>

<P>
<FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="2">benefits of holding index funds can be even greater, as our funds' low turnover generally
results in fewer realized capital gains. <br><br>

<B>It pays to invest for the long run</B><br><br>

Of course no one knows what will happen in the financial markets in 2006 and
beyond. That uncertainty is one reason we always encourage our shareholders to
evaluate their investments from a long-term perspective. It's also why we place
such high value on what experience has shown us are the keys to a successful
long-term investment program--namely, balance among stock, bond, and money
market funds; a disciplined approach to investment selection; a constancy of
purpose that doesn't shift with market trends; and careful attention to costs.
As an investor, you, too, can weather the market's uncertainties by sticking with a
well-planned strategy. Investing in Vanguard's large-cap index funds is a
smart way to capitalize on the stock market's long-term potential. In fact, these
funds--with their diversification, low turnover, and low costs--offer a useful
model for managing all your investments.<br><br>

Thank you for entrusting your assets to Vanguard.<br><br>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Major Left Bold-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Growth Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares,
Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who
meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.
Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and
servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading
on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements. <br><br>1. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Security Valuation:
          Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange
          (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are
          valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from
          the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on
          the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked
          prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or
          whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the
          fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary
          markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair
          value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that
          fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to
          maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a
          matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields,
          maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.
          Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which
          approximates market value.<br><br> 2. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures
          contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure
          to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing
          transaction costs. The fund may purchase or sell futures contracts to achieve a
          desired level of investment, whether to accommodate portfolio turnover or cash
          flows from capital share transactions. The primary risks associated with the use
          of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values
          of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>3.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements. <br><br>4.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>27 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
<!-- MARKER PAGE="sheet: 1; page: 1" -->
<HR SIZE=5 COLOR=GRAY NOSHADE>

<br><br>




<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Head Left-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="1" COLOR="#FF0000">Growth Index Fund </FONT> </P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>5.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional
          borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured
          at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities
          loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity
          Fund, and records a liability for the return of the collateral, during the
          period the securities are on loan. Security lending income represents the income
          earned on investing cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>6.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income
          includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and
          is accrued daily. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities
          are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale
          of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.<br><br> Each class
          of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class
          separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of
          shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and
          shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each
          class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income,
          other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are
          allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>B.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The Vanguard Group furnishes at cost investment advisory, corporate management,
          administrative, marketing, and distribution services. The costs of such services
          are allocated to the fund under methods approved by the board of trustees. The
          fund has committed to provide up to 0.40% of its net assets in capital
          contributions to Vanguard. At December 31, 2005, the fund had contributed
          capital of $1,243,000 to Vanguard (included in Other Assets), representing 0.01%
          of the fund&#146;s net assets and 1.24% of Vanguard&#146;s capitalization. The
          fund&#146;s trustees and officers are also directors and officers of Vanguard.
          <br><br><B>C.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net
          investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes.
          Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are
          reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their
          tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income,
          expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial
          statement and tax purposes; these differences will reverse at some time in the
          future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of
          short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Default" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>During the year ended December 31,
2005, the fund realized $4,667,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind
redemptions&#151;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the
fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not
distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized
gains to paid-in capital. <br><br>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2005, the fund had $365,000 of
ordinary income available for distribution. The fund had available realized losses of
$3,559,058,000 to offset future net capital gains of $316,442,000 through December 31,
2008, $1,752,289,000 through December 31, 2009, $747,930,000 through December 31, 2010,
and $742,397,000 through December 31, 2011. <br><br>At December 31, 2005, net unrealized
appreciation of investment securities for tax purposes was $2,956,317,000, consisting of
unrealized gains of $3,184,325,000 on securities that had risen in value since their
purchase and $228,008,000 in unrealized losses on securities that had fallen in value
since their purchase. </FONT></P>

fund&#146;s Forms N-Q on the SEC&#146;s website at www.sec.gov. Forms N-Q may also be
reviewed and copied at the SEC&#146;s Public Reference Room (see the back cover of this
report for further information). </FONT></P>

<H1 ALIGN=LEFT><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE="3" COLOR="#FF0000"><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B> </FONT> </H1>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Vanguard Value Index Fund is
registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 as an open-end investment company, or
mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, Admiral Shares,
Institutional Shares, and VIPER Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who
meets the fund&#146;s minimum purchase requirements. Admiral Shares are designed for
investors who meet certain administrative, servicing, tenure, and account-size criteria.
Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative and
servicing criteria and invest a minimum of $5 million. VIPER Shares are listed for trading
on the American Stock Exchange; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2><B>A.</B>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted
          accounting principles for U.S. mutual funds. The fund consistently follows such
          policies in preparing its financial statements. <br><br>1. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Security Valuation:
          Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange
          (generally 4:00 p.m. Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are
          valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from
          the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on
          the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked
          prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or
          whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the
          fund&#146;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#146; primary
          markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair
          value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that
          fund&#146;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to
          maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a
          matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields,
          maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services.
          Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which
          approximates market value. <br><br>2. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures
          contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure
          to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing
          transaction costs. The fund may purchase or sell futures contracts to achieve a
          desired level of investment, whether to accommodate portfolio turnover or cash
          flows from capital share transactions. The primary risks associated with the use
          of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values
          of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the
          possibility of an illiquid market.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para Flush Lv 0-Arial" FSL="Project" -->
<P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>Futures contracts are valued at their
quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate principal amounts of the contracts are not
recorded in the financial statements. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are
recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of
Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when
they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses). </FONT></P>

<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Project" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>3.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated
          investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Accordingly, no
          provision for federal income taxes is required in the financial statements.<br><br> 4.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend
          date.</FONT></P>


<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Para (List) Flush Lv 0- Arial" FSL="Default" -->
     <P><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=2>5.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
          Security Lending: The fund may lend its securities to qualified institutional
          borrowers to earn additional income. Security loans are required to be secured
          at all times by collateral at least equal to the market value of securities
          loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market</FONT></P>



<!-- MARKER FORMAT-SHEET="Page Number Center" FSL="Project" -->
<P ALIGN=CENTER><FONT FACE="Arial, Helvetica, Sans-Serif" SIZE=1>46 </FONT></P>
<DIV STYLE="page-break-after:always"></DIV>
